item.title: Kerry Prize Bond holder scoops €500,000
item.description: Christmas has come early for one prize bond holder in Kerry, as the monthly prize of half a million euro – tax free - has been scooped in the county. The winning prize bond number was ADG 508 969, which was purchased in 2016. There were over 8,700 (8,755) prizes awarded in this week’s draw, amounting to more than €1.2 million (€1,233,475). item.title: Gardaí appealing to motorists in Kerry to take care on roads over Christmas period
item.description: Gardaí are appealing to road users in Kerry to stay safe over the festive period. Regional Chief Superintendent for the Southern Garda Region, Colm O’Sullivan made the plea. Figures presented by the Chief Superintendent show an increase in road traffic incidents in the county this year. item.title: Gurney exits World Championship
item.description: There's plenty of Irish interest at the final day of World Darts Championship action before the Christmas break. Derry's Daryl Gurney lost the deciding set to Callan Rydz. This evening, Limerick's Willie O'Connor faces three-time champion Michael van Gerwen. Advertisement While World number 11 Josh Rock plays Joe Comito in tonight's final match. Two-time champion Peter Wright is out after losing 3-nil against Germany's Arno Merk.

item.title: Research finds Kerry among the counties least likely to complete the 12 pubs of Christmas
item.description: Kerry has been ranked as one of the counties where peope are least likely to complete the twelve pubs of Christmas. That’s according to research conducted by Casino.org Ireland, based on data from the 2022 Census, Garda statistics and liquor-licence counts. The report shows that Kerry ranks 23rd out of 26th in likelihood to complete the crawl, with a 1-in-5 chance of people making it to pub number 12. item.title: Council to seek meeting with Uisce Éireann to discuss lack of water in Kenmare and impact on development
item.description: The council is to seek a meeting with Uisce Éireann to discuss the lack of water in Kenmare and the impact it’s having on developments in the area. The issue was raised at the recent Kenmare MD meeting by Independent councillor Dan McCarthy. In September, it emerged that developers of multi-unit housing projects in Kenmare must now also supply the water. item.title: Slight drop in number of flu cases in Kerry
item.description: There was a slight drop in the number of flu cases recorded in Kerry last week. That’s according to data from the Health Protection Surveillance Centre. It shows there were 105 recorded cases of the flu in Kerry between 13th and 20th December, down from 136 the week before. Advertisement The rate of cases per 100,000 population also decreased, from 86.9 last week to 67.1.
